newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Traub starts composition process.
newsitem.headline: German Traub starts composition process.

text.p: German machine tool maker Traub AG on Tuesday announced that it would apply to begin composition proceedings -- the German system's final layer of defence against bankruptcy.
In a mandatory statement, Traub said all its activities would continue to operate as normal and that its goal was to return to lasting profitability as soon as possible.

Traub said it had initiated the composition proceedings -- in which banks join with the company to assess its balance sheet in an attempt to reorganise its debt and ensure its survival -- because its units were insolvent.

Such news had been broadly expected after Traub's shares were suspended for two days beginning on Monday at the request of Deutsche Bank AG, which is the leader of a banking pool which held talks on Monday with the company.
Traub appealed to its shareholders, staff, associates and banks to support its initiative for survival.

"The goal of the process is to return Traub to lasting profit as soon as possible. Restructuring measures already completed or still ongoing in a bid to improve operating results will play a decisive role in this," Traub said.

The composition proceedings cover Traub AG and its Traub Drehmaschinen GmbH and Traub-Heckert Vertribs GmbH units. A drop in orders had caused Traub's net loss to double to 16.4 million marks in the first half of 1996.
The company last week said it had sold off a substantial share of its 50 percent stake in German firm Hermle AG in one of a series of planned measures to shore up its cash position.
